# ADR 0013: Project structure is generated by xcodegen from project.yml, not hand-maintained

## Context
ADR-0004 fixed the shape of the Xcode project: one app target, one widget-extension target, one
local Swift package (`MissionControlKit`) with six library targets. Building that structure means
either hand-editing `MissionControl.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj` (a large, merge-hostile, easy-to-
corrupt XML/plist-like format with no meaningful diff) or generating it from a small declarative
spec. This walking-skeleton spike is also the first time any Xcode project exists in this repo at
all, so whatever's chosen here is what every future infrastructure/widgets/service-integrations
task will build on top of.

## Decision
`MissionControl/project.yml` is the source of truth for target structure, dependencies,
entitlements wiring, and build settings (bundle IDs, deployment target, signing style/team,
Info.plist keys including the widget's `NSExtensionPointIdentifier`). `xcodegen generate` (Homebrew:
`brew install xcodegen`) turns it into `MissionControl.xcodeproj`. Both `project.yml` and the
generated `.xcodeproj` are committed to git — per ADR-0011's "Cmd-R is the whole deploy loop," a
fresh checkout must build and run without first requiring a separate `xcodegen generate` step or
installing xcodegen at all. `project.yml` stays authoritative for structural changes: after editing
it, regenerate and commit the result.

Signing is `CODE_SIGN_STYLE: Automatic` with `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM` set to the resolved Team ID
(`2C553PK57P`, from the paid Apple Developer Program membership behind the "Apple Development:
loreema2800@icloud.com" identity already in this Mac's login keychain) — this selects automatic
signing with a specific team, it does not hardcode a signing identity string. Verified via
`xcodebuild -showBuildSettings | grep -i team`.

## Consequences
### Positive
- `project.yml` diffs cleanly in code review; `project.pbxproj` diffs do not.
- Adding a target/dependency/entitlement is a few YAML lines instead of manual Xcode UI
  clicking that's easy to get subtly wrong (e.g. forgetting to also add an entitlement to the
  widget extension target, which ADR-0007 explicitly requires from day one).
- Reproducible: anyone (including a future agent task) can regenerate an identical project from
  the spec, which also makes it easy to verify structural claims (e.g. "the widget extension does
  not link MCPersistence") by grep'ing one file instead of the pbxproj.

### Negative
- One more tool dependency (xcodegen) for anyone who wants to modify structure, not just build.
  Mitigated by committing the generated project so building never requires it.
- Two files must stay in sync (`project.yml` and the generated `.xcodeproj`) — a `project.yml`
  edit without a re-`generate` silently does nothing. No automated check enforces this yet; worth
  a pre-commit hook if this becomes a recurring mistake.

### Neutral
- This doesn't change anything ADR-0004 already decided about target *shape* — it's purely how
  that shape gets materialized into Xcode's project format.

## Alternatives considered
- **Hand-maintain `project.pbxproj` via Xcode's GUI only** — rejected: no reviewable diff, and
  every future infra task that touches project structure (a new widget kind, a new library
  target) becomes a manual, error-prone Xcode-UI exercise with nothing to check it against.
- **Tuist** (another declarative-project-generator) — not evaluated in depth; xcodegen was chosen
  for being simpler (single YAML file, no separate manifest DSL to learn) and sufficient for this
  project's modest target count. Revisit if the project ever needs Tuist-specific features
  (module graphs at Tuist's scale, plugin system).
- **Swift Package as the whole app** (no `.xcodeproj` at all, an executable SPM target) — rejected:
  WidgetKit extensions and App Group / Keychain-access-group entitlements need Xcode's build
  system and a real `.appex` bundle; plain `swift build` cannot produce that.
